The kettle sings, a thin, high voice of necessity. Ramesh offers the liquid, the steam, the warmth, but the solid grain is absent. Ramesh speaks the truth of the situation with the blunt clarity of a man who has been ignored. The Directorate demands vouchers for every rupee of the state's money, yet my own body demands sustenance and they have not paid the man who cooks. It is a contradiction in the administration of the household, a private state failing in its ethical duties because the public state has failed in its bureaucratic ones. The steam rises, a thin column of spirit escaping the material pot. It is a small, immediate negation of the heavy haze pressing against the windows, a breath of the universal in a particular cup. I will sit and let the moment be what it is, a pause in the motion of my debts and delays.

Ramesh retreats to the back, leaving me with the silence and the haze. I have not eaten in over a day, and the body is a stubborn fact that resists the spirit's indifference. I cannot think clearly on an empty stomach, nor can I continue to ignore the basic mechanics of my existence here.

works.to: The Officer in Charge, Directorate of Estates
works.tail:

I request that the necessary corrections be made to the files so that the residence may be formally allocated to its proper occupant. In the interim, I shall continue to manage the household affairs, including the payment of the dhobi and the electricity, using the imprest funds provided. I am careful to distinguish between the state’s money, which requires vouchers, and my own cash, which is limited. This distinction is vital; the ethical fabric of the household, like that of the state, depends on the clear separation of particular and universal duties.

I trust this matter will be resolved in the course of the day, as all particulars must resolve into the universal. I remain, with respect, your obedient servant,

Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
Resident, Tughlak Road
